I'm 50 this year, been farming these 7.8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My father farmed this same land before me. I finished primary school — can read prices at the shop and sign my name, but I don't mess with complicated calculations. My wife and I do the farm work, my son works at a factory in Handan and only comes back for wheat harvest and busy times. We have five mouths to feed including my daughter who's still in school. Money is always tight.

I have 5 mu in wheat-maize double crop and 2.8 mu in cotton. The wheat is already in the ground from last fall — I planted it around October 12th with the improved seed, same as every year. Now in spring I need to think about the topdressing and first irrigation. Last year the wheat gave me about 900 jin per mu, decent. For fertilizer, I put down base fertilizer before sowing — about 30 kg of compound and 10 kg of urea per mu. At jointing in late March I'll spread another 15 kg of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang cut his fertilizer by one bag last year to save money and his wheat was short and yellow, only got 700 jin. I'm not making that mistake — better to waste a little fertilizer than lose half the crop. I irrigate three times: once now at regreening, once at jointing, and once at flowering. The pump electricity bill hurts but dry wheat means no yield.

After wheat harvest in early June, there's barely a week before I must plant maize. I hire Old Liu's no-till planter for 40 yuan per mu — no time for plowing. Maize must be hybrid seed, can't save it, so I buy Zhengdan 958 from the county shop, 80 yuan per mu. At planting I put compound fertilizer in the furrow, about 40 kg per mu, then topdress with 20 kg of urea when the corn is knee-high. Two irrigations for maize if the summer rains don't come — one after planting if it's dry, and one when the tassels come out. I expect about 1000 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

The 2.8 mu cotton is my wife's responsibility. We plant in late April. Cotton needs more babysitting — thinning, weeding, spraying for bollworm three or four times. I use the improved cotton seed, 50 yuan per mu. Fertilizer is lighter than the grain crops — about 30 kg of compound and 10 kg of urea per mu for base, then another 8 kg of urea at flowering. We irrigate twice. The problem is picking — with my son away, it's just my wife, my mother, and me. Last year we hired two women from East Village for the third and fourth picking, paid them by the jin. We'll probably need to hire again this year, which costs but we have no choice. I hope for about 1200 jin of seed cotton per mu.

Total cash I have for inputs is about 6000 yuan. Fertilizer is the biggest bite — need over 2000 yuan worth. Seed is another 800, irrigation electricity maybe 900, pesticide 800, machine hire 200, and hired pickers probably 500. My wife wants to keep 1000 yuan aside for my daughter's school fees and medicine, so I cut back a bit on the cotton topdress fertilizer. Wheat and maize are more reliable, they get priority. I reckon I'll spend about 5200 yuan total on inputs this year.
